english: Let $k$ be the real number for which the system of equations
has a non-trivial solution. For this value of $k$, the number of solutions $(x,y,z)$ of the system in which $x$, $y$ and $z$ are integers with $|x|\le1000$, $|y|\le1000$ and $|z|\le1000$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $k$ वह वास्तविक संख्या है जिसके लिए समीकरण निकाय
का एक अतुच्छ (non-trivial) हल है। $k$ के इस मान के लिए निकाय के उन हलों $(x,y,z)$ की संख्या, जिनमें $x$, $y$ तथा $z$ पूर्णांक हैं तथा $|x|\le1000$, $|y|\le1000$, $|z|\le1000$ है, ______ है।
solution: Then equation 3 coincides with equation 1; from equations 1 and 2: $x:y:z=\begin{vmatrix}1&-1\\-3&2\end{vmatrix}:-\begin{vmatrix}2&-1\\1&2\end{vmatrix}:\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\1&-3\end{vmatrix}=-1:-5:-7$
solution_full: A homogeneous system has a non-trivial solution exactly when its coefficient determinant is zero.
For $k=2$ the third equation is the same as the first, and the first two are independent, so the solutions form a line through the origin.
Cross-multiplying the first two equations: $x:y:z=(2-3):(-1-4):(-6-1)=-1:-5:-7=1:5:7$. So the solutions are $(t,5t,7t)$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$.
Since $x=t$, the solution is an integer triple exactly when $t$ is an integer.
The bounds: $|t|\le1000$, $|5t|\le1000$, $|7t|\le1000$; the last is the strongest, $|t|\le\frac{1000}{7}=142.8\ldots$, so $t=-142,\dots,142$.
That is $2\cdot142+1=285$ solutions, the trivial solution $(0,0,0)$ included.
originality_note: New: after the homogeneous condition fixes k, the solution line is intersected with an integer box, so the count depends on the primitive direction (1,5,7) and the largest coordinate (way 5). Closest known: find k for which a homogeneous system has a non-trivial solution. Different because: the question continues to the structure of the solution set and a lattice-point count.
blueprint_concepts: Solving system of homogeneous linear equations

concept_use.Solving system of homogeneous linear equ: Coefficient determinant 2 - k = 0 gives the non-trivial case k = 2; the solution set is then the line (t, 5t, 7t), counted in the box.

stem_review: Read as a student: k is unique (determinant linear in k); 'solutions in which x, y, z are integers' includes the trivial one, stated in the solution; bounds are inclusive. Checked by enumeration: 285. Answer 285, a positive 3-digit integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: k = 2 from the determinant, solutions t(1,5,7), count integer t with |7t| <= 1000.
justification: Routine chain: a 3x3 determinant, a cross-multiplication and a short count. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2) in length.
